aiReadyLines.text: Sample Question lil
Read the text and answer the questions 5, 6 & 7
On May 29, 1953, Sir Edmund Hillary from New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay, a
Sherpa climber from Nepal, became the first to successfully reach the summit of
Mount Everest, the world's highest peak at 8,848 meters (29,029 feet). Their historic
climb was part of a British expedition led by John Hunt.
The journey to the top of Everest was extremely challenging. Harsh weather, freezing
temperatures, and thin air made the climb dangerous. However, with determination and
teamwork, Hillary and Tenzing managed to overcome these obstacles. Finally, after
weeks of climbing, they stood at the summit, becoming the first humans to conquer
Their achievement was celebrated worldwide. Edmund Hillary was later knighted by
Queen Elizabeth II, and Tenzing Norgay became an international hero. Their climb
remains an inspiration for adventurers and mountaineers across the globe, proving that
with courage and perseverance, even the greatest heights can be reached.

On May 29, 1953, Sir Edmund Hillary from New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay, a
Sherpa climber from Nepal, became the first to successfully reach the summit of
Mount Everest, the world's highest peak at 8,848 meters (29,029 feet). Their historic
climb was part of a British expedition led by John Hunt.
The journey to the top of Everest was extremely challenging. Harsh weather, freezing
temperatures, and thin air made the climb dangerous. However, with determination and
teamwork, Hillary and Tenzing managed to overcome these obstacles. Finally, after
weeks of climbing, they stood at the summit, becoming the first humans to conquer
Everest.
Their achievement was celebrated worldwide. Edmund Hillary was later knighted by
Queen Elizabeth II, and Tenzing Norgay became an international hero. Their climb
remains an inspiration for adventurers and mountaineers across the globe, proving that
with courage and perseverance, even the greatest heights can be reached.
